summary: Follow-up on the 2026-09-02 production incident where Orion experienced increased token latency and intermittent 5xxs. Redwood reviewed root cause analysis (allocator bug + degraded KV cache hit rate), proposed mitigations (allocator patch, throttling, alert tuning, autoscale policy adjustments), and agreed on staged rollouts and artifacts to share (traces, replay instructions, SOC2/KMS docs).
topics: Root cause: allocator concurrency bug + KV cache degradation
Short-term mitigations: throttling, temporary model pinning, manual cache priming
Long-term fixes: allocator patch, improved alerting and SLA thresholds, autoscale tuning
Security/compliance questions: KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 supplement
Next steps: artifacts to share, staging replay, timeline for patch rollout
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the postmortem follow-up for the Sep 2 incident and make sure next steps are clear.
[00:12] Tom (Orion): Thanks Jenna, yeah we got hit pretty hard during our morning batch - latency spiked and a bunch of requests returned 5xx. We had to failover to the backup model which helped but cost us throughput.
[00:30] Marcus (Redwood SE): quick note - in the RCA we saw two correlated issues: an allocator concurrency regression when request concurrency exceeded our knob, and a drop in KV cache hit-rate due to a cache-eviction pattern after a busy window.
[00:46] Priya (Orion): when you say allocator, is that the token allocator inside the runtime or something at the infra layer? we noticed pods were OOM-ing in one AZ.
[00:58] Marcus: it's in the runtime layer - there was a race that occasionally allocated a big scratch buffer for certain attention patterns, which pushed memory over the soft limit; kube then started evicting and that caused the cache to cold start, so you see the cascade.
[01:18] Luis (Security): any chance this was triggered by malformed inputs or adversarial traffic? we have compliance folks asking.
[01:28] Marcus: we scanned request payloads around the window, no malformed highlights; patterns were high concurrency and atypical long sequences from a queued job - not suspected adversarial.
[01:36] Jenna: to add, our alerting didn't trip early enough - the 95th pct latency climbed for a few minutes before the pager. we need better early-warning thresholds.
[01:48] Tom: yes the first alert came after the Failover. by then we had degraded customer SLAs.
[02:02] Marcus: short-term mitigations we applied: pinning the workload to a lighter model variant, increasing throttle on bursty routes, and manual cache priming on the affected pods. That bought time while we prepared a patch.
[02:28] Priya: pinning helped but we still saw occasional errors in the tail. any ETA on a permanent patch?
[02:36] Marcus: we have a PR that fixes the allocator race; it requires a small choreography change in the allocator's freelist. we propose staged rollout: canary 10% in staging tomorrow, 30% in prod next week, full rollout after verification.
[02:54] Jenna: timeline-wise we suggested canary 9/13, prod 9/15-9/17 depending on replay results.
[03:03] Tom: ok. we need traces and logs to correlate with our internal telemetry - can you share filtered traces and pointer to the span ids?
[03:12] Marcus: yes i'll collect the request traces, the runtime traces, and pod logs. we'll redact PII and provide direct links to the otel traces.
[03:22] Olivia (CSM): also we'll include a short how-to for running the traffic replay in your staging environment, with the exact payloads and sequencing we observed.
[03:34] Luis: about security/compliance - our security team wants to confirm KMS usage for model keys and audit log retention. does Redwood have a KMS integration guide?
[03:44] Jenna: yes we do, we'll share the KMS/HSM integration guide and the SOC2 supplement doc. note that for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM options; for hosted we have envelope encryption with customer KMS options.
[04:03] Priya: one more - RBAC changes? we saw a spike in token-level requests, want to make sure principle-of-least-priv is enforced for the replay artifacts.
[04:12] Marcus: we'll provide shareable links with read-only roles and time-limited tokens for the traces.
[04:20] Tom: good. can we also get recommendations for autoscale policies? we hit a sudden throttle and the autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough.
[04:29] Marcus: yes we recommend adjusting the target utilization and adding a proactive buffer for your peak windows - in your case, target util at 60% with a 30% burst headroom and shorter scale-up window. we'll attach a suggested policy.
[04:45] Priya: curious - did the KV cache degradation mean we need more memory per pod or a different eviction policy?
[04:53] Marcus: the eviction was due to the OOM cascade; patching the allocator reduces transient memory spikes, but for long-term we suggest increasing kv cache allocation for that route and switching to an LRU with TTL to avoid synchronized evictions during bursts.
[05:10] Tom: ok - what's the impact on cost if we increase cache size or provision more headroom?
[05:17] Jenna: small increase in per-token cost due to larger working sets, but the cost of frequent failovers and customer SLA breaches is higher. Redwood Optimize can run a quick simulation to quantify cost vs latency tradeoff.
[05:33] Luis: any tradeoffs around dedicated vs hosted for this sort of workload? we might consider Dedicated because of predictable capacity.
[05:42] Jenna: Dedicated would give you reserved GPU pools and more control over autoscaling settings. It also reduces noisy-neighbor risks and gives stronger isolation for cache warmness; but it comes with commit costs.
[05:57] Tom: probably worth a conversation with finance; let's get the facts first.
[06:05] Marcus: back to rollout - after the patch canary, we'll run the replay in staging (you Tom/Priya will run it), we'll validate 95pt and error rates, and then roll to prod incrementally. we'll also tune alerts to raise earlier.
[06:20] Priya: how will we know the alert thresholds to set? can you give sample SLO thresholds?
[06:27] Marcus: yes, we'll provide suggested SLOs: 95th latency under 250ms for our lighter model on typical requests, 99th under 800ms, error rate <0.1% - these are starting points for your traffic pattern.
[06:44] Olivia: i also want to flag the need for a runbook update - who owns the runbook change? Marcus, can you propose the steps to remediate if this reoccurs?
[06:52] Marcus: yes i'll draft a runbook section: immediate throttling, model pin, cache priming, and how to toggle allocator fallback.
[07:03] Tom: excellent. also, we want a postmortem writeup that we can share internally - simple timeline, root cause, mitigations, owners.
[07:11] Jenna: we'll circulate a short postmortem doc by 9/12 once Marcus uploads traces.
[07:20] Priya: any other fleeting effects we should watch for after patch? e.g., latency regrowth or small memory leaks?
[07:28] Marcus: we'll monitor memory and open a small stress test to look for leaks; part of canary will include longer-run heap profiling.
[07:38] Luis: does this change any of our compliance posture? i.e. will logs or traces include sensitive tokens?
[07:45] Jenna: we will redact tokens and PII from shared artifacts; production audit logs remain in your tenant and are unaffected.
[07:52] Tom: ok, timeline recap?
[07:55] Marcus: collect traces & logs by 9/12, postmortem doc by 9/12, canary in staging 9/13, staging replay by 9/17, prod rollout 9/15-9/17 depending on replay success.
[08:10] Olivia: i'll set a follow-up call for 9/18 to review staging results and sign off on prod.
[08:18] Tom: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:22] Jenna: thank you, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[08:30] [meeting ends - note: 48 min call in platform meta]
